descriptor: Long reads on coast, craft and local mysteries

voice.summary: The Skerrow Review sounds like a good magazine essayist: patient sentences, a dry aside now and then, and respect for the reader's time. Interface text stays low and neutral so the article can speak.
dos: Write headlines as concrete scenes, not claims
Keep interface labels to one plain word
Let the first sentence carry a small hook
donts: Use clickbait phrasing or numbered listicle titles
Explain the reading controls at length

taglines: Stories from the edge of the map
Set the type, keep the thread
A good lamp and a better story
boilerplate: The Skerrow Review publishes long-form features on coastal life, local lore and unexplained habits, with a reading view the reader can tune to their own eyes.

microcopy.error: We lost your place. Scroll to carry on.

logo.note: An open book is the honest symbol for a publication built around reading comfort.
